title: What Happens When Your Ears Pop?
sources: Mayo Clinic, 'Airplane ear' (airplane ear happens when the air pressure in the middle ear and the air pressure in the environment don't match; a narrow passage called the eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the back of the nose and throat and regulates the pressure; the mismatch keeps the eardrum (tympanic membrane) from moving as usual; rapid pressure changes during climb or descent can outpace the tube's ability to adjust; swallowing or yawning opens the tube so air can enter the middle ear and equalize pressure; symptoms: ear discomfort, fullness or stuffiness, muffled hearing; self-care: yawn, swallow, chew gum or suck candy; see a doctor if discomfort, fullness or muffled hearing lasts more than a few days or symptoms are severe): https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/airplane-ear/symptoms-causes/syc-20351701 (text verified via the Mayo Clinic Care Network health library mirror)

Cleveland Clinic, 'Eustachian Tubes' (the tubes run from your middle ears to the back of your nose and throat; they close when you're not swallowing or yawning and should only open when you yawn, chew or swallow; they equalize air pressure in the middle ear and drain fluid): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/22072-eustachian-tubes

Cleveland Clinic, 'Eustachian Tube Dysfunction' (the tubes connect your middle ears to the back of your throat; most common symptom is muffled hearing, almost like you're underwater; clicking or popping sounds; home remedies: chew gum, yawn, swallow; see a provider if symptoms last longer than a couple of weeks): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/22527-eustachian-tube-dysfunction

Indiana Public Media / Indiana University, 'A Moment of Science: What makes our ears pop?' (the eustachian tube is normally closed; to equalize pressure it has to open, and the pop comes with that opening): https://indianapublicmedia.org/amomentofscience/what-makes-our-ears-pop.php

Tease (next video): Mayo Clinic, 'Muscle cramp' (a sudden, unexpected tightening of one or more muscles; occurs mostly in leg muscles, most often in the calf; usually lasts seconds to minutes): https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/muscle-cramp/symptoms-causes/syc-20350820

lines.text: What happens when your ears pop?
That pop is a hidden tube opening inside your head.
lines.caps: THAT *POP IS | A HIDDEN *TUBE | *OPENING INSIDE | YOUR *HEAD

lines.text: Behind each eardrum sits a pocket of air,
linked to your throat by that tube, which usually stays shut.
lines.caps: *LINKED TO YOUR | *THROAT BY | THAT *TUBE | WHICH *USUALLY | STAYS *SHUT

lines.text: On a plane, air pressure changes faster than the tube can adjust,
lines.caps: ON A *PLANE | AIR *PRESSURE CHANGES | *FASTER THAN | THE TUBE CAN *ADJUST

lines.text: so your eardrum can't move right, and everything sounds muffled.
lines.caps: SO YOUR *EARDRUM | CAN'T *MOVE RIGHT | AND *EVERYTHING | SOUNDS *MUFFLED

lines.text: Then you swallow or yawn, the tube opens,
air slips in, and pop, the pressure evens out.
lines.caps: AIR *SLIPS IN | AND *POP, THE | PRESSURE *EVENS OUT

lines.text: Still sore or muffled days later? See a doctor.
